title: Building AI Agents that actually automate Knowledge Work - Jerry Liu, LlamaIndex
talk_summary: Jerry Liu argues that automating knowledge work requires a strong preprocessing/toolbox layer over unstructured documents (parsing, extraction, indexing, specialized tools) plus a deliberate split between unconstrained 'assistant' agents and constrained 'automation' agents that run in the background with batch human review. The concrete evidence is mostly about document/Excel parsing accuracy, not about agent orchestration, review gating, or model routing.

takeaways.technique: Constrained automation agents as backend, unconstrained assistant agents as frontend
takeaways.what_they_do: They separate background, batch-triggered automation agents with explicitly defined control flow and end-of-run batch review from chat-style assistant agents that use open ReAct loops with heavy human steering; automation agents structure data and expose tools the assistant agents consume.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the architecture is a little bit more constrained which kind of makes sense right? If you want this thing to run more end to end um you need it to not just go off the rails

takeaways.technique: Specialized tools over a semantic map instead of raw code-writing
takeaways.what_they_do: For messy Excel, they first build a semantic map of the sheet structure, then expose that as a set of specialized tools to the agent, rather than letting the LLM write code from scratch over raw text/CSV.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're helping it out by really providing uh a set of specialized tools over the semantic map so you can reason over an Excel spreadsheet
takeaways.numbers: LLM+code interpreter baseline 70-75% accuracy; their specialized-tool approach 95%; human baseline 90%

takeaways.what_they_do: They insist on a real preprocessing layer — connectors, permission/metadata sync, document parsing/extraction — before any indexing or tool exposure, because bad parsing makes even a great LLM fail.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the documents are not processed correctly, no matter how good your LLM is, um it will fail

takeaways.technique: Batch review at end of automation runs
takeaways.what_they_do: Automation agents run end-to-end with less human-in-the-loop per step, but route output to a batch review stage before downstream action/approval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's usually a little bit less human in the loop at every step of the process and usually some sort of like batch review in the end
